structure.title: Causal-learn: Causal Discovery in Python
structure.fit: First small-scale structure baseline: PC-stable plus kernel CI under causal sufficiency; FCI plus kernel CI for latent-confounding equivalence-class output. Low-dimensional event-level variables fit better than high-dimensional waveform graph learning.
structure.limits: FCI requires causal Markov/faithfulness, valid CI tests and appropriate independent rows. It outputs a PAG, not guaranteed exact DAG, nor a causal effect or proof that hidden confounding is absent. KCI is cubic in row count. Do not treat repeated events as independent CI-test rows.
structure.background_knowledge_source_audit: Tag0.1.4.8 FCI.py lines245-267 turns a forbidden X->Y relation on an existing adjacency into the opposite directed edge with a tail. Encoding merely 'later Y cannot cause earlier A' by forbid(Y,A) would impose A->Y and can erase latent-confounding-compatible endpoints. Use no BK initially; keep temporal knowledge separate until endpoint semantics are validated. This is an input-semantics limitation, not a performance-failure claim.
structure.decision: Recommended baseline pilot; no adoption claim. Pin exact tag if later installed. Report CPDAG/PAG endpoints rather than coercing all edges to DAG.

structure.title: Score matching through the roof: linear, nonlinear, and latent variables causal discovery
structure.maintenance: Archived2025-03-12; research reproduction repository,2 visible commits; README usesPython3.12.5.
structure.license: Repository badgeMIT-0; inspected score_independence.py SPDX saysMIT. Preserve both if later reusing, no source copied here.
structure.assumptions: Score/Hessian criteria use positive differentiable density. Stronger directed-edge identification assumes C3 additive observed and latent mechanisms, independent positive-density noise, and non-Gaussian noise for linear arguments; see Section2, Proposition1 and Assumption1.
structure.fit: Interesting recent research comparator for smooth continuous SCM diagnostic controls; weaker linear/nonlinear restrictions than original SCORE.
structure.task_mismatch_inference: Current cumulativeY has atoms at0 and sometimesT, with Bernoulli/Beta generation and quantized10s outcomes. These do not directly satisfy the stated positive smooth continuous-density additive-noise model. Adding jitter or discarding zeros would alter the data/problem, not establish assumptions.
structure.decision: Reserve, not first main method on current bounded zero-massY. Could compare only in a separately declared smooth-ANM diagnostic, not claim full task coverage.

structure.title: Ordering-Based Causal Discovery for Linear and Nonlinear Relations
structure.maintenance: 7visiblecommits; precise latestdate not verified. Research repository usesR-dependentcdt/CAM pruning, increasing adaptation cost.
structure.assumptions: Section3.1 PDFpage3 assumes no unobservable confounder and Gaussian additive independent noise. Assumption1 PDFpage4 gives sufficient identifiability via non-decreasing noise variance or sufficiently strong effects. Nonlinear/linear mixture does not remove these conditions.
structure.fit: Mixed linear/nonlinear smooth-ANM comparator; parent score relates to derivative-based effect magnitude under its assumptions.
structure.decision: Not first taskbaseline: latentconfounding and bounded zero-massY conflict with core assumptions; parent score is not automatically causal factor contribution for our data.

structure.title: DAGMA: Learning DAGs via M-matrices and a Log-Determinant Acyclicity Characterization
structure.maintenance: 109visiblecommits; exact latestdate not verified. Numpy/scipy/igraph and nonlinear torch-based model ecosystem; no install performed.
structure.fit: Mature differentiable acyclicity optimizer supporting linear/nonlinear continuous score models and binary logistic models.
structure.limits: Acyclicity constraint ensures a DAG-shaped fitted structure, not uniqueness/causal identifiability under arbitrary hidden confounding. Separate binary support does not automatically provide a correct zero-inflated bounded continuous likelihood.
structure.decision: Reserve causal-sufficient comparator; not selected solely for producing a complete directed graph.

structure.title: FoundCause: Causal Discovery with Latent Confounders from Observational Data
structure.publication: arXiv2606.17516v1,2026-06-16; no peer-reviewed venue independently verified
structure.maintenance: Archived2026-06-17 for exact reproduction; README says PRsnotaccepted. v1.0releaseJune17,commitbf21a29.
structure.cost: RepositoryREADME: pretrainedcheckpoint about1.6GB/139Mparameters; torch and schedulefree among dependencies; CPUoptionavailable. Not downloaded or run.
structure.fit: Recent amortized transformer trained on syntheticSCMs, predicts directed edges and hidden-confounder scores. Research benchmark claims include latentconfounding, so worth a later task-matched comparison.
structure.limits: Repository lists training2-50variables,100-600samples, observational-only input. Predicted confounder scores are learned-pattern predictions rather than a proof of latent identification or removal; benefit on our zero-mass, repeated-user data untested.
structure.decision: Latest reserve, not initial4-variablepilot priority because adaptation and checkpoint cost exceed established FCI baseline.

structure.title: Assessing the Overall and Partial Causal Well-Specification of Nonlinear Additive Noise Models
structure.license: NoLICENSEfile or reuse license verified at repository entrance; no code copied
structure.maintenance: 185visiblecommits; exactlatestdate not verified. R software usesFOCI andxgboost; authorREADME notes FOCI with ties can be nondeterministic and ignoreRseeds.
structure.fit: Methodological reference for testing whether nonlinear/additive causal modeling is well specified, rather than accepting every fitted graph as mechanism evidence.
structure.decision: Use theoretical guidance, reserve implementation pending license and bounded/tied-outcome applicability; do not make it an initial dependency.

derivative.title: Doubly Robust Inference on Causal Derivative Effects for Continuous Treatments
derivative.status: arXiv preprint; v2 2025-04-18; author publications page still lists it under Preprints; no formal journal publication verified
derivative.replication_repository_license: No separate explicit license verified; use the MIT package source for permitted reuse
derivative.decision: Best matched new use: estimate marginal compensation effect directly. First do a formula microcheck; retain existing DR curve as current main method.
derivative.fit: Targets derivative of population causal mean under identification/smoothness/support assumptions. Conditional effect modification does not identify causal effects of the conditioning variables themselves.
derivative.positivity_exception: The without-positivity branch adds an additive structural outcome assumption; it cannot generally accommodate arbitrary compensation-by-state interactions or recover unsupported heterogeneous curves.
derivative.implementation_cost: Low for independent CPU formula with supplied nuisance values; medium with cross-fitted spline/Ridge nuisance learning. Author package imports torch even for sklearn branch. No package was installed.

derivative.title: Causal Inference with a Continuous Treatment: Addressing Positivity Constraints, Nonlinearity, and Effect Heterogeneity
derivative.license_and_maintenance: Replication entrance verified; package license and version not independently inspected, no code reused
derivative.contribution: Explains how nonlinear dose response and pretreatment effect heterogeneity can be observationally indistinguishable when treatment ranges differ strongly across groups. Small additive-shift targets can require less extrapolation.
derivative.decision: Use its identification lesson and same-observations/different-counterfactual example. A local shift is an optional additional estimand, not a replacement of the user's required continuous amount curve.

derivative.title: Parameterizing the effect of a continuous treatment using average derivative effects
derivative.contribution: Efficient density-free estimators for weighted scalar average derivative effects using Riesz representations and local overlap. The estimand generally differs from an unweighted population derivative curve.
derivative.decision: Reserve for a compact sensitivity summary when a weighted scalar target is substantively useful; does not provide the required whole curve or its local threshold.
derivative.cost: Author R research code with mgcv/ranger/SuperLearner and other dependencies; medium-high integration cost relative to formula microcheck

derivative.title: Debiased inference for a covariate-adjusted regression function
derivative.license: Unresolved: DESCRIPTION retains literal template use_mit_license(), use_gpl3_license() or friends to pick a license; no explicit top-level license verified. Do not describe repository as MIT/GPL or copy its code without clarification.
derivative.contribution: Explicit local-polynomial smoothing-bias correction for a covariate-adjusted mean curve, with pointwise/difference and uniform-band inference under stated conditions, avoiding undersmoothing.
derivative.decision: Strong later candidate for principled whole-curve and level-set threshold inference. Independently implementing paper mathematics is possible; current conditional multiplier bands do not already constitute this method.
derivative.cost: R package depends on nprobust/SuperLearner and several learners. Medium-high for full reproduction, no installation attempted.

derivative.title: Data-Driven Uniform Inference for General Continuous Treatment Models via Minimum-Variance Weighting
derivative.author_code: No author repository independently verified at paper entrance
derivative.license_and_maintenance: No reusable code license or maintenance record verified
derivative.contribution: Minimum-variance balancing weights with a closed-form sieve solution, local-linear generalized dose-response estimation, bootstrap uniform bands and bias-control tuning.
derivative.decision: Reserve alternative; it is not a new DR uniform estimator. Its Section 2 explicitly leaves doubly robust GDRF/uniform inference to future work. Higher independent reproduction cost; do not transplant its guarantee onto current DR.

derivative.title: Debiased inference for proximal dose-response function
derivative.fit: Targets dose-response and first derivative under unmeasured confounding using distinct treatment-/outcome-inducing proxies and bridge functions, with explicit smoothing-bias correction.
derivative.decision: Not first implementation: current EV schema has no validated pair of proximal proxies. Current I/P channels or Y>0 cannot simply be declared suitable proxies. Relevant only if the needed variables and identification assumptions become defensible.
